chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Minqari, from Isa al-Zaif, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man kills a man deliberately, what is his repentance?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He makes himself available (to the guardians of the killed one)'. I said, 'He fears that they would kill him'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him give them the wergild (blood money)'. I said, 'He fears that they would come to know him due to that'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him consider the wergild, so let him make it as small packages, then await the timings of the Prayers, so let him cast these in their houses'.
ai.seo_question: What is the repentance for a man who kills someone deliberately according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific legal mechanism for a deliberate murderer to achieve repentance by offering himself to the victim's heirs (al-awliya) for execution or blood money. It provides a nuanced practical solution for the killer who fears retaliation, allowing him to discreetly pay the diyah by breaking it into small bundles (surar) and placing them in the heirs' homes during prayer times, thereby fulfilling the financial obligation without necessarily exposing himself to immediate death.
